payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k-1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.

dependency_self_check.boundary_case_check: At t=(n-1)/n and k=n, kt=n-1 so the formula still gives floor(kt)=n-1.
dependency_self_check.lemma_used: Directly proved the stated floor identity for all admissible n,t,k.
range_checks: Used only n>1, (n-1)/n <= t < 1, and 1 <= k <= n.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, and let t be any real number with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

From t >= (n-1)/n, we get
k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, so k - k/n >= k-1. Therefore
k-1 <= k t.

On the other hand, t < 1 implies k t < k.
Thus
k-1 <= k t < k.
Because k-1 is an integer, this interval condition implies floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary in {1,2,...,n}, the conclusion holds for every such k.
result_payload.proof_summary: For k<=n and t in [(n-1)/n,1), one has k-1 <= kt < k, hence floor(kt)=k-1.

used_external_facts: Basic characterization of the floor function: if m is an integer and m <= x < m+1, then floor(x)=m.
